summary: docs/BIOME_TRAITS.md sections 2, 4 and 6 are implemented in PainterIO.Core and tested. New folder Core/Traits: TraitId (binding values 1-8) and TraitKind, TraitSpec (data, NaN parameter = TraitDefaults value, Clone), RuleTraits (Classic, one spec per id where the last given wins, disabled specs kept but inert, Has / Get, canonical ToKey 'Id(p1,p2);...' of the enabled traits in id order, Parse accepting 'classic' / '' and lenient tokens, value Equals, Clone, With), ISimTrait (exact section 4 signature) plus the optional ISpeedTrait, TraitRegistry (ApplyConfig for Inertia / SparkSpeed / ArcReach / RingInterval on the CLONED SimConfig, CreateBehaviours in TraitId order), TraitDefaults (catalogue, defaults, validation) and one file per behaviour trait: CoalescenceTrait, PropagationTrait, ScorchedEarthTrait, ConductionTrait. SimConfig gains Traits (default RuleTraits.Classic, deep-copied by Clone) and ContactScale (ContactRadius = (HeadRadius + TrailHalfWidth) x ContactScale). The Simulation constructor applies the config traits to its clone, then creates and attaches the behaviours and checks HeadGrace > PawnSpeed x (largest speed factor) x Dt. Hooks sit at the section 6 points: SpeedFactor in step 1 (Conduction, whole tick), AugmentCapture in step a for unchased returns before the R18 conflict rule (Coalescence, cells sorted and de-duplicated, part of Return.Cells), OnEliminated after Neutralize and before the Eliminated event (ScorchedEarth), EndOfTick in step 3 after sparks and before the ring spawner (Propagation, ScorchedEarth bookkeeping); trait events are emitted after the hooks. SimEventType.TerritoryGrew is appended at the END. SimView gains Traits, IsScorched(cell), plus ScorchEndTime(cell) and HomeSpeed for wave D-2. StateHash adds the trait key and the running scorches only when a trait is enabled. Bots read every value from SimConfig and account for Conduction (plan budget for the transit to E on own land, waypoint pass radius at home, intercept time with the own-land part at PawnSpeed x factor) and for ArcReach (shorter approach). Classic stays bit-identical: every trait code path is skipped when Traits is classic. Evidence: 7 full bot rounds (60, 30 and 144 Hz, lasso on/off, human slot or not) reproduce the rolling StateHash recorded with the Gate C Core before any change, and the whole existing suite (316 tests) is green unchanged. Tests: 83 new cases (one file per trait, RuleTraits key round trip, classic equality, every trait alone and each biome set in bot rounds with invariants every tick, EventCapHits == 0, twin-run determinism, cross-rate equality at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz for SparkSpeed, ArcReach, RingInterval, Coalescence and Propagation). dotnet loop (tools/CoreTests, .art/traits-core): 399 / 399 green. Unity EditMode through the lock: 586 cases, 583 passed, 2 skipped (existing BotsReport human-proxy), 1 failure outside this package (WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount on LiquidComposite, the in-progress F2 drop shader of another package); all 83 trait cases and all 168 older Core cases pass in Unity. Balance report (50 seeds, lasso off, bot-only): the safety assertions hold for every set (TimeUp 90-98 %); 3 of 5 expected tendencies are met with the section 3 defaults (Feu highest passive growth, Electricite most cuts and most saved chases). 2 are missed (Feu kill share 46 % ties Liquide 47 %; Liquide is not the closest to classic) because Inertia(420) alone raises the kill share from 31 % to 49 %. With Liquide Inertia 480 and Feu SparkSpeed 2.3, all 5 are met, lasso off and on (diagnostic runs, see balance_report). I did NOT change the defaults: this is a proposal for the user.

contract_issues: R1 vs Propagation: section 2 says 'every NEUTRAL arena cell', so a territory next to the rim grows into the outer band of cells that R1 says 'stays neutral forever (puddles never touch the rim)'. Implemented as written. Implied amendment: R1's sentence holds only without Propagation, and the D-2 renderer must accept puddles that reach the rim. The alternative would restrict Propagation to cells whose center lies inside the inset shape (SignedDistance <= -ArenaMargin); that is a user decision. Capture semantics stay sound (Void cells are still 'outside').

Propagation, reading of 'cells under any live head': the head's current Cell plus every cell whose center lies within HeadRadius of the head center (the pearl disc). The own-trail exclusion uses GridRaster.RasterPolyline of the trail (it ends at the head after step 3) plus the cells of its first and last points, then their 4-neighbours.

Propagation timing and order (as built): it grows at the tick end where floor(t / Interval + 1e-9) increases (at most once per tick). TerritoryGrew carries Time = the tick end time and comes after the event-loop events and before RingSpawned, one event per player in player order, Cells ascending. It never runs once the round has ended, so a TimeUp at a multiple of Interval grows nothing (the scores are final). Rings > 1: each ring is computed on the grid left by the previous one, all in one event. Only alive players claim.

Coalescence readings (as built): a hole is a 4-connected component of neutral cells whose outside 4-neighbours are all the returner's cells after ITS capture. A rival or Void neighbour, or a neighbour outside the territory box, means it is not enclosed. The captures of simultaneous returners are ignored for the enclosure; R18 then settles contested cells. The area test is strict (count x CellSize^2 < MaxHoleArea): 127 cells are filled, 128 cells (2.0 u^2) are not. Holes that existed before the return are filled too, and an unchased return that captured nothing still fills holes. Scorched cells count in the enclosure and area test but are never filled; the other cells of such a hole are.

ScorchedEarth readings: IsScorched(cell) = the cell is neutral and Time < EliminatedAt + Duration. A captured scorched cell is no longer scorched, and freeing it again scorches it anew (the later end time wins). Inside step a the trait clock is the group time (Simulation.TraitTime), so the scorch test stays rate independent.

StateHash salt definition (section 4 says only 'the trait key and the scorch state'): when a trait is enabled, the hash adds the key length, the key characters, and for every running scorch its end time (rounded to 1e-9) and freed cell count. So a traited round never shares a hash with a classic one, even when the state is the same (tested with Inertia at 540 deg/s).

HeadGrace check: the largest speed factor comes from attached behaviours implementing the new optional ISpeedTrait (ConductionTrait: max(1, factor)). The check runs after Attach, at the end of the constructor; the classic check on the caller's config is unchanged and stays first.

TraitSpec / RuleTraits details beyond section 4: NaN parameters mean the defaults; enabled specs are validated (finite; SparkSpeed > 1; Propagation Interval > 0 and Rings in [0, 64]; Conduction and ArcReach > 0; the others >= 0), disabled ones are not. ToKey always prints both parameters ('Inertia(420,0)'). Parse also accepts numeric ids, bare ids (defaults) and one parameter, and throws FormatException otherwise. The RuleTraits constructor throws ArgumentException.

Conduction applies for the WHOLE tick that starts on own land, including the exit tick. Factors of several speed traits multiply. With HomeSpeedFactor >= SparkSpeedFactor, the closed-form catch of a cut made in that exit tick falls back to EventResolver's 'spark not faster than the pawn' branch for that one tick. Validation does not forbid this combination; the defaults (1.3 vs 1.5 / 2.1) are far from it.

Bots and ArcReach: section 4 lists 'contact radius' among the values bots read. The intercept estimate now subtracts the extra reach ContactRadius - (HeadRadius + TrailHalfWidth), which is exactly 0 in classic rounds.

Section 6 expected tendencies with the section 3 defaults: 'Feu has the highest kill share per cut' is MISSED (Feu 46 % vs Liquide 47 %, lasso off; 44 % vs 56 % lasso on) and 'Liquide stays closest to classic' is MISSED (relative distance L 0.218, F 0.201, E 0.151). Cause: Inertia(420) alone raises the bot kill share from 31 % to 49 %, because the bots' escape estimate ignores turning time. Proposed table change for the user (section 3, Runtime BiomeTraitTable): Liquide Inertia(480) and Feu SparkSpeed(2.3). Measured: lasso off, 50 seeds, Liquide kill 38 % with distance 0.115 and Feu kill 49 %; lasso on, 20 seeds, Liquide 44 % with distance 0.172 and Feu 49 %. All five tendencies are then met. Defaults NOT changed.
Brief / v1.4 unchanged: chased returns still capture nothing with every trait (Coalescence fills nothing on a chased return, tested). Traits never test a biome id (Core has no biome).

Alternative to the Inertia change (not done, it would alter classic bots unless gated): add the turning time to the bots' escape and return estimates.

open_issues: Coalescence has no measurable effect in bot-only rounds (identical aggregates to classic over 50 seeds). Holes appear mainly when an island rival is eliminated or Propagation leaves contested cells. Liquide's gameplay identity rests on Inertia. If a stronger liquid feel is wanted, MaxHoleArea could be raised (5 u^2 also fills 2 x 2 u holes); that is a design decision.
Inertia and Conduction are tick-rate dependent by design (documented in their test files, as for turning). The other five traits have cross-rate tests.

The dotnet Core loop now takes about 3.5 min on this machine (was about 1 min), mostly the balance report (4 sets x 50 seeds lasso off + 4 x 20 lasso on) and the 11 trait-set rounds. Under Unity the balance report runs 2 seeds per set and the trait-set rounds last 30 s (they took 7.8 s in total in the EditMode run).

The probe hashes per biome (section 6 'Player' line) need the D-2 Runtime wiring (BiomeTraitTable, -classic / -traits / -trait flags in Probe and DevShot); Core is ready. Classic probe hash 246577239DE179C4 is expected unchanged: the classic Core is bit-identical (pinned by TraitsClassicTests on 7 bot rounds), but I did not run the player probe in this package (no Runtime change, no build).
needs: Wave D-2 Runtime (not this package): Runtime/Biomes/BiomeTraitTable.cs with the section 3 table. Tests/EditMode/Core/Traits/TraitTestKit.cs carries a copy of the section 3 keys for the Core tests (LiquidKey, FireKey, ElectricKey); a Runtime EditMode test should check that BiomeTraitTable's defaults equal those keys, so the two copies cannot drift. If the user accepts the proposed tweaks, both must change together.

Wave D-2 Runtime: TerritoryField should treat SimEventType.TerritoryGrew like a fill from the territory edge (reveal times), build _PIO_ScorchMask from SimView.IsScorched / ScorchEndTime (fade over the last 2 s), and use SimView.HomeSpeed or Config.Traits for the Conduction streak. Note: TerritoryGrew is stamped with the tick END time and comes after the event-loop events of that Step (like RingSpawned).
Wave D-2 Runtime: GameSession must set SimConfig.Traits per round. Probe and DevShot default to RuleTraits.Classic (the SimConfig default), so the classic hash needs no Runtime change.
